Raymond James: In the 4Q25 call (period ended December 2025), the firm stated it has invested in AI to help advisers save time, make better decisions and be more efficient in their operations with their clients.

The comparison of which firm makes the most extensive or strongest claims cannot be ranked on a single shared scale: the firms' claims differ in definition, scope, and metric. Morgan Stanley's CEO makes the most categorical framing, calling AI existentially important and absolutely the top priority for the firm as the adviser, and saying it is now double overweight (MS-TR-2026Q3#49); Bank of America reports the largest deployment figures (300-plus approved use cases, 200,000-plus teammates using AI, 400,000 prompts a day: BAC-TR-2026Q2#6); Schwab reports the most use cases among firms that state a count in the same unit (more than 220 use cases: SCHW-TR-2025Q4#18) versus Bank of America's 300-plus approved use cases (BAC-DECK-2026Q2#29), but these counts are not on the same basis (approved vs. in-use vs. use cases in development). No single firm's claims are comparable against the others for a definitive ranking.
